# SPD-013 — Token and cost accounting per member and per ticket

## Brief
[[SPD-007]] stores what the Agent tool returns per member (`total_tokens`, `duration_ms`, `tool_uses`, `usage_json`), and the subagent transcripts carry per-message usage. This ticket adds per-ticket rollups, cost from a per-model price table, and a cost column on the card from [[SPD-010]]. Evidence: the spike's probe 2 `tool_response` and the transcript `usage` fields.

Priority lowered from Vitelotte's suggested P2 to P3: nothing depends on it, and Eric has not asked for cost.

Done when: `spud card SPD-nnn` shows tokens and cost per member and a total per ticket.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, the persona tier, no children. The data side (what the transcript sum keeps, and a re-sum of stored rows) would take fable, but Eric ruled Fable out (2026-09-13), so the engineer proves the sums against the real transcripts read-only and Spud reviews at return. Eric decided the cost basis at start (2026-09-13): the API list price in USD, labelled as list price so it is never read as his subscription's bill, from a dated per-model price table in `spud.config.json` that he can update. Design decided at start: the transcript sum keeps a per-model breakdown, with cache writes split by TTL (5 minutes, 1 hour) and server-tool requests; cost is computed at render time from that breakdown and the table, so a price change only re-renders; `member resum` adds the breakdown to a stored sum; a member whose models are not all priced shows no cost, and a ticket total over it says it is partial. `spud card` shows tokens and cost per member and a total per ticket; the Team table gains a cost column and a total row, and the member note a `cost_usd` key. The engineer names the price table's block, with its source and date, and Spud pastes it into `spud.config.json` at merge, since the config is Spud's file. [[SPD-022]] and [[SPD-017]] run in Eric's other session and change the same file, so the importer change stays small.
